newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says trapped miners alive after seven days.
newsitem.headline: Peru says trapped miners alive after seven days.

text.p: Two miners trapped underground for a week after a powerful earthquake in southern Peru are still alive, officials said on Tuesday.
"The latest information is that they are giving signals to show they are still alive," said Rosario Guevara, Civil Defence spokeswoman.
Firefighters and journalists, however, said the sounds -- supposed to be the men banging rocks to communicate with their rescuers -- were echoes of noises made elsewhere in the mine.
The miners were believed to have survived on small rations of food and water they had taken into the gold mine at Guanillo, near Nazca, 290 miles (460 km) to the south of Lima.
Experts said they could survive one more day underground.

The quake that shook southern Peru last Tuesday measured 6.4 on the Richter scale. It killed 14 people, injured hundreds and left tens of thousands homeless. Most of the damage was caused in Nazca where many houses were destroyed.
The quake killed a miner at Moyohauca, 375 miles (600 km) south of Lima, in the department of Arequipa, and tens more had to be dragged out of several remote mines around Nazca.
